title: What's Focal Is Casual
coreMove: Separate what is most visible from what is actually causing the result.
sourcePressure: The source says channeled attention can make a visible feature feel causal, so what is focal can be mistaken for what explains the outcome.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: If something keeps appearing in the story, it must be the reason the story happened.

hook: An abstract claim that attention changes everything
A generic meeting where someone makes a better pitch
A clever sentence about persuasion before any concrete object appears
counterintuition: You think persuasion happens during the ask, but it happens before it
The obvious factor is not always the important one
Influence is not manipulation when used well
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on attention
Write down three ways to be more persuasive
Ask yourself what matters most right now

exampleSpecs.audience: an operations manager reviewing a late-bag complaint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the visible carousel jam is mistaken for the true staffing cause
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager traces timestamps backward from the jam to the unstaffed transfer belt before assigning blame
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a frozen baggage carousel with one suitcase wedged sideways

exampleSpecs.audience: a risk analyst explaining a spike in declined payments
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the most obvious country flag becomes the false cause
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the analyst hides the country column and shows device fingerprints first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dashboard row of red declines with one flag column minimized

exampleSpecs.audience: a grower diagnosing wilted basil trays
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the visible yellow leaves distract from a pump timer error
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the grower points the apprentice to the dry irrigation line before they cut open another leaf
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rows of basil trays sagging under glass

exampleSpecs.audience: a producer reviewing why listeners quit mid-episode
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one awkward joke gets blamed instead of the ad break placement
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the producer plays the retention graph muted, then reveals the joke happened after the drop
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a waveform frozen at minute nineteen

exampleSpecs.audience: a technician investigating cracked appliance handles
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the cracked plastic gets blamed instead of packing pressure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the technician stacks shipping inserts by lot number until the focal crack no longer looks like the cause
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three cracked handles lined under a bench lamp

exampleSpecs.audience: a curator explaining cloudy tanks to donors
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the visible haze is mistaken for neglect instead of a filter-cycle change
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the curator shows the maintenance chart before letting donors stare through the clouded glass
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a viewing window with silver fish moving through haze

skillTargets: test alternate causes hidden outside the spotlight
avoid blaming the most photographable feature
redirect attention toward evidence that explains the result

tryThisNowSpec: Take one problem you are explaining and write the most visible feature beside the least visible possible cause, then decide what evidence would separate them.
